title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
hook: Treat a robot's actions as just more text tokens, and a vision-language model can learn to act — carrying its web knowledge into the physical world.
key_points: Co-fine-tunes internet-pretrained vision-language models jointly on robot trajectories and vision-language tasks.
Expresses robot actions as text tokens, so language and action share one model.
Improves generalization to novel objects and commands not seen in training.
Enables multi-stage semantic reasoning via chain-of-thought — the 'VLA' idea.
content_html: Anthony Brohan, Noah Brown, Justice Carbajal, and colleagues introduce RT-2, which co-fine-tunes vision-language models — pretrained on internet-scale data — jointly on robot trajectory data and ordinary vision-language tasks. The trick: robot actions are expressed as text tokens, so a single model handles both language and action. This is the vision-language-action, or "VLA," model idea.
extra_html:
How it works

Rather than bolting a separate controller onto a perception model, RT-2 folds action directly into the same vocabulary the model already uses for text. Actions become token sequences, and training mixes robot trajectories with web vision-language data so the model never forgets what it learned from the internet. Because one model carries both kinds of knowledge, web-scale understanding flows into how the robot decides what to do.

Why it matters

Sharing a model between language and action pays off in generalization. RT-2 handles objects it never saw during robot training, interprets commands outside its demonstration set, and can chain multi-stage reasoning through chain-of-thought before acting. By turning a vision-language model into an actor, it shows how internet-scale knowledge can transfer into physical control — extending the scaling story RT-1 started.

related.hook: Connect a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM with just a linear projection, fine-tune on GPT-4-generated image dialogues, and get a capable open chat-with-images model for under a day of training.

related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.
